Create a container without starting it (like `docker create`). Pulls the image and persists the config; launch it later with `carrick start`

Usage: carrick create [OPTIONS] <IMAGE> [COMMAND]...

Arguments:
  <IMAGE>
          

  [COMMAND]...
          

Options:
      --platform <OS/ARCH>
          Target platform, e.g. `linux/amd64` or `linux/arm64`. Selects the OCI manifest entry for multi-arch images. Defaults to the host-native architecture, so it is not needed for a native run (arm64 on Apple Silicon, amd64 on the x86_64 lanes). On Apple Silicon, `linux/amd64` runs the x86_64 guest through Apple Rosetta 2 and requires it to be installed

      --store <STORE>
          [env: CARRICK_HOME=]

  -t, --tty
          Allocate a pseudo-terminal and run interactively (like `docker run -it`)

  -i, --interactive
          Keep STDIN open even if not attached (like `docker run -it`)

      --fs <FS>
          Which writable-layer backend to use. Defaults to `host`. The in-memory backend (`memory`) is opt-in (`--features fs-memory`)

          Possible values:
          - host: Host-APFS passthrough via cap-std: the kernel is the single fork-coherent source of truth. The only backend in a default build

      --exec-backend <EXEC_BACKEND>
          Execution backend policy. `native` is experimental and trusted-code-only
          
          [env: CARRICK_EXEC_BACKEND=]
          [default: hvpatch]
          [possible values: hvpatch]

      --pid <PID>
          PID namespace mode (like `docker run --pid`). `private` (default) runs the container in its own PID namespace (init is pid 1); `host` shares the host PID namespace (no remap)

          Possible values:
          - private: A fresh PID namespace (default; `docker run` default)
          - host:    Share the host PID namespace (`docker run --pid=host`)
          
          [default: private]

      --pull <PULL>
          Docker `--pull` policy: `always` re-checks the registry and re-pulls a moved tag, `missing` (default) pulls only when the image is absent, `never` uses only the local cache
          
          [default: missing]
          [possible values: always, missing, never]

      --net <NETWORK>
          Container network mode: host, bridge, none, or container:<id|name>
          
          [default: host]

      --network-alias <ALIAS>
          Add a service alias on the bridge network

      --ip <IPv4>
          Assign a static IPv4 address on the bridge network

      --add-host <HOST:IP>
          Add a custom host-to-IP mapping in the guest's /etc/hosts

      --dns <IP>
          Set a custom DNS nameserver

      --dns-search <DOMAIN>
          Set a custom DNS search domain

      --dns-option <OPTION>
          Set a custom DNS resolver option

  -e, --env <KEY=VALUE>
          Set environment variables

      --env-file <FILE>
          Read in a file of environment variables (may be repeated)

  -w, --workdir <DIR>
          Working directory inside the container

  -u, --user <USER>
          Username or UID

      --entrypoint <COMMAND>
          Overwrite the default ENTRYPOINT of the image

  -v, --volume <host-src:container-dest[:ro|rw]>
          Bind mount a volume

      --volumes-from <CONTAINER[:ro|:rw]>
          Mount volumes from another container

      --mount <type=bind,source=host-src,target=container-dest[,readonly]>
          Attach a filesystem mount to the container

      --name <NAME>
          Assign a name to the container

      --rm
          Automatically remove the container when it exits

      --stop-signal <SIGNAL>
          Signal to stop the container (name like `SIGQUIT`/`TERM` or number). Overrides the image's `STOPSIGNAL`; defaults to `SIGTERM`

      --stop-timeout <SECONDS>
          Seconds to wait for the container to stop before SIGKILL (used by `stop`/`restart` when `-t` is not given). Defaults to 10

  -p, --publish <hostPort:containerPort>
          Publish a container's port(s) to the host (no-op under host networking)

      --security-opt <OPTION>
          Docker-compatible security options. Supported: `seccomp=unconfined` (disable the launch-time default syscall policy — carrick's model of Docker's builtin seccomp profile) and `seccomp=default`/ `seccomp=builtin`. Custom profile files are not supported

      --cap-add <CAPABILITY>
          Docker-compatible `--cap-add`: grant a capability beyond the container default set, by its `capabilities(7)` name without the `CAP_` prefix (`SYS_ADMIN`, `SYS_PTRACE`, `SYS_NICE`, ...). Repeatable. Docker's default bounding set drops most capabilities AND its seccomp profile is capability-conditional, so this both raises the modeled set and lifts the launch-time denials that capability gates

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
